item.title: Finding Faults with Thermal and Spectral Imaging: From Radiometry to Equipment Selection
item.description: Visible cameras answer “is it there, what is it”; thermal cameras answer “where is it hot, how hot”; spectroscopy answers “what material, is its state normal”. Failing equipment leaves different traces in the three channels: a loose joint heats up first, degrading insulation discharges first (UV), damp materials change their spectral reflectance first. My two earlier posts — the dual-spectrum camera survey and the embedded integration walkthrough — covered the cameras and the plumbing; this one covers the last mile: using temperature fields and spectra to find problems, and how to pick equipment for that job. The order: thermometry physics → thermal signatures of faults → industry criteria → spectral methods → equipment requirements and selection → reading methods and automation.
